header.name: Asian Paints Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Asian Paints (NSE: ASIANPAINT) makes and sells paints and home decor products; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹35,584 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹9,977 crore, 16.9% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 12.5% against 14.0%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹1,068 crore, 7.5% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 29 Oct 2026, the first session after the result, ASIANPAINT shares rose 0.76% while the NIFTY 50 rose 1.05% and the NIFTY INDIA CONSUMPTION index rose 1.05%; allowing for the market's move, ASIANPAINT's own move was -0.35%, about 0.28 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the consumption (thematic) sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹2,573 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), a discounted cash flow model with a 11.18% cost of capital does not reach the price at any revenue growth up to 30% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 15.4%; nor, with revenue growing at its FY23–FY26 rate of 1.0%, at any operating margin up to 60%.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to the cost of capital (one percentage point either way: a model value of ₹444 to ₹592 a share) and to the operating margin (two percentage points either way: a model value of ₹447 to ₹565 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹5k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of ASIANPAINT's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.what: Revenue grows only at FY26's pace for five years, the operating margin slips 2 points, and growth after year 10 earns no more than its cost of capital.

scenarios.name: Base

flags.title: The price is beyond what the model can reach
flags.text: The model cannot reach the price at any revenue growth up to 30% a year, so the page says 'more than 30%' instead of forcing a number. No operating margin up to 60% reaches it either. This is a statement about the model's range and assumptions, not a forecast and not a view on the shares.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 2 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

flags.title: A tax line was keyed wrongly for FY22
flags.text: The exchange file for the year to March 2022 reports a tax expense of the wrong sign and size, which overstates that year's profit. It is shown as explained, not repaired, and that year is outside the history the valuation uses.

flags.title: Lease lines read from scans
flags.text: Lease lines come from scanned results documents. They were machine-read and checked against the printed subtotals, and are marked as not yet checked by a person.

limitations: Template A (non-financial, positive free cash flow). Single-stage fade model; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Asian Paints' exchange XBRL files fold lease liabilities into other financial liabilities at every date. The lease lines come from the results PDFs, which are scanned documents: the figures were machine-read and checked against the printed subtotals and the XBRL totals.

The XBRL for the year to March 2022 carries a keying error in the tax expense and profit for the period of its annual column; the error is listed, not corrected, in the reconciliation report, and that year is outside the history the valuation uses.
The sector comparison uses the Nifty India Consumption index, a thematic index, because the paints business has no sector index of its own in this project.

At the valuation date the model does not reach the share price at any revenue growth or operating margin inside the ranges it searches. That is a statement about the model's ranges and assumptions, not a view on the shares.
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
